significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that "reversal rate scales with the target language's reliance on non-word-order cues ... not with resource level," together with the form-(ii) mechanism that a shared "role-binding" representation causally carries and can reverse agent/patient assignments. This establishes both a predictive cross-language phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining which languages should fail, why cue conflict causes failure, and whether apparent transfer reflects shared role semantics or imported surface heuristics; that distinction is load-bearing given the language-specific cue weighting formalized by MacWhinney's Competition Model and the shared syntactic structure reported by Chi et al., "Finding Universal Grammatical Relations in Multilingual BERT" (ACL 2020). Verified false and verified true are distinguishable: failure of the cue-distance relation would rule out dominant-language cue-hierarchy import in favor of target-language-faithful or resource-linked accounts, although failure to localize the compact representation alone would only reject the proposed mechanism. In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of shared versus language-specific multilingual representations would merit only the topic median; the specific cue-distance-over-resource law and causal role-binding account are what raise this score.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the "per-language cue-hierarchy index" coupled to "reversal rate" as a diagnostic/predictor, plus the "role direction" as an intervention for repairing or inducing reversals. The cue-distance relation is ex ante because it predicts which case- or voice-dominant languages require stress testing before deployment, whereas the recovered role direction is mainly a post-hoc, per-model intervention after the failure mode has been identified. After model-specific re-extraction, the steering vector itself must be rediscovered, but the asserted relation that cue-hierarchy distance—not resource level—predicts reversals would still tell auditors and multilingual evaluation builders what to expect across model families and language classes. The topic-substitution check lowers the generic multilingual-transfer topic to 5; the named forward-looking screening rule and its uptake by people who audit or gate models justify the higher reach, though the absence of a model-independent intervention or demonstrated outside-AI action window keeps it below 9.
